lead: the work that comes in is sized to a place with staff — a second bench, somebody answering the phone. what is here is you, until two in the morning, doing every part of it by hand.
sun: nobody has asked how many of you there are. the estimate gets made at the door, at a width you did not choose, and it prices the workshop rather than the pair of hands. so the jobs arrive in volume, at the delivery dates a firm would quote, and you take them, because taking them is what a place that size does. the work goes back on time and the estimate is never corrected.
moon: your hands take up whatever is put down near them, without weighing it first — that part has never needed deciding — so the volume goes through and comes out finished, and nothing in you keeps a total of what has left. thirty years of it and there is no book anywhere. what people have of yours is in their kitchens. what you have is the next one, already started.
pull: they price the workshop and the hands do the work, and the hands are two, and no one who has ever handed you a job has had a reason to learn that.
tension: the delicate job goes to somebody else, and nobody decided that. it does not occur to anyone holding a small careful thing to bring it to the largest maker in the county, so twenty years of bulk has come in and the commission your hands are best at has been placed four times elsewhere. you watched three of them do it. you were pleased for them, you would have been better, and saying so at your size is not available.
cost: the volume of a firm goes through one bench and comes back on the date quoted, every time, which is why nobody has ever needed the arrangement explained. hands wear at the ordinary rate of hands, though, and nothing stands behind these two. a bad wrist takes out everything anyone thinks you are, and the size would go on being quoted for years after the bench went cold.

lead: eleven months went into it, and the first person to see it finished said it looked like it came easily, and meant that warmly, and everyone since has said a version of the same thing.
sun: the reading of you is finished before the work is in the room. it was taken in a doorway, at a size nobody consulted you about, and it sits higher than anything you have made — so what you bring gets checked against it instead of looked at. the checking comes out fine every time. that is why no one has had to look.
moon: the thing itself is good, and it goes out bare — no preface, no case made for it, nothing put around it to tell a stranger what they are holding. next to a reputation that arrived first, bare reads as casual. so the work confirms what was already decided instead of meeting it, and the eleven months are nowhere in the object where anybody could find them.
pull: The Mane got there first and the work came in behind it, so everything you make now lands as evidence of something the room had settled before it saw anything of yours.
tension: the compliment is always some version of easy, and it comes warmly, from people with no reason to flatter you. every hour that went in is taken out by it. the correction would be naming the hours, which at your scale plays as angling, so the hours stay where they are. and nothing you finish arrives as an achievement — an achievement wants somebody to be surprised, and no room has been surprised by you in twenty years.
cost: nothing you make has ever needed a case built around it first — no framing, no managing the room, none of the apparatus that keeps other people from working — so the hours all went into the making. a size like yours reads as supply. four things are what you have actually finished, and every person handling one is handling it as though the next is due in the spring.

lead: the person introducing you gets four words in, stops, and hands it over to you. what you give back is not an answer either, and the room takes that for discretion and moves on to the drinks.
sun: at this scale a room cannot leave you unaccounted for. somebody has to be able to say what you are before the evening starts, and the size guarantees the question gets asked — so the answer gets supplied for you. a committee you sat on once becomes the place you are from. it travels in that form for a decade, and nobody passing it along has needed to check.
moon: you were never with any of it. no roll, no side, no house that could produce a letter about you — and none of that has registered as a loss from inside, which is why the invented placements stand. correcting one would take wanting a real one, and nothing in you has gone looking for a real one since you were old enough to be asked.
pull: everyone can pick you out and nobody can place you. the answer they use was invented by somebody kind, years ago, and it has been travelling on its own ever since.
tension: nobody lowers the reading when they cannot find what it rests on. they assume the base is private — an arrangement, an old family, a post too well-mannered to mention — and what comes back is respect for a discretion you are not exercising. no arrangement exists to be discreet about. said out loud at your size, that sentence is the most elaborate version of the same discretion, and it has never landed as the plain fact it is.
cost: admission arrives without credentials — no letter, no membership, nobody vouching for you — and it has saved you the twenty years other people spend earning a seat. nothing sits under the seat. on the day something goes badly there is no house whose business it is to stand behind you, and everyone who might have helped assumes, from the size, that a bigger one already has.

lead: his side of it is the thing you cannot put down, held at the same weight as your own, two years into a fight the room settled long ago as a big party leaning on a small one.
sun: nothing you do in this reads at its own size. a letter from you is a manoeuvre. a month of saying nothing is pressure being applied. turning up in person is the whole animal in the room, whatever you came to say. no lower setting exists for any of it, so the record fills up with acts that were ordinary when you did them and are large by the time anybody reads them back.
moon: both hands closed early and neither has moved since — one on the claim, which is sound, and one on the fact that he is owed something, which is also sound. from inside there has never been a wobble in that; it has never felt like doubt. a settlement would need one hand to give, and winning would need you to stop believing half of what you know.
pull: you are holding your case and his case, and neither hand will open, and a grip that patient reads to everyone watching as a large party waiting for a small one to run out.
tension: people who have not read a line of the correspondence call it throwing your weight around. the weight is the estimate, and the estimate is the one item in this you did not build. insisting at that size that you are ordinary is the least believable sentence available, and every attempt at it improves his case by a little. so the fairness stays in you, unusable, and the file goes on looking exactly like what everyone says it is.
cost: you can sit across from someone who wants everything you have, hold his account of it, and come back next month unmarked — none of the wear this normally puts on a person. the steadiness is the exhibit. every month you last is read as a month you could afford to lose, and calm that costs you nothing is the best evidence anyone has that you started with more.
